# Discovery corpus

**Every file here is SYNTHETIC**, generated by `tools/gen_discover_corpus.bas`
in the gBASIC tree. No real account, member, employee or institution data.

Copied from `examples/fixtures/ari_discover/`, same author, same licence.

## Why the ARI fixtures are not this corpus

`tests/fixtures/` holds three report fixtures, **two of which are the same
report**. Variation across files is what separates a true constant from an
accidental one, and three sources cannot supply it: at that size
`minimum_support: 0.80` means "3 of 3", so 0.80 and 0.95 are the same
threshold. Testing Phase 0 there would test it against data that cannot
distinguish the thing Phase 0 exists to distinguish.

## One declaration produces both the report and the truth

`truth.json` is written by the same program that writes the reports, from the
values it **planted** — never read back out of the text it printed. A
hand-written answer key drifts the first time either side changes, and *a
fixture whose answer key is wrong teaches the tool to be wrong and then
certifies it.*

| set | sources | what it measures |
|---|---|---|
| `*.rpt` + `truth.json` | 24 branch-activity reports over nine declared drift axes | furniture precision **and** recall by line number; row-family recall; the planted values themselves |
| `null/` | 12 structureless noise sources | **false positives.** The right answer is zero furniture lines. This is what caught a defect that invented pages in 14 of 18 single-page sources, and nothing else in the suite could have |
| `adversarial/non_ascii.rpt` | names carrying `Ç`, `Ü`, `Å` | the byte/codepoint split. Every other fixture is pure ASCII, where the two index spaces coincide — so the corpus **cannot** catch a mixed-up offset without this file |
| `adversarial/fixed_width_gap.rpt` | a column whose values never reach its heading | positional inference failing silently |
